answer: The potter fires only pots stamped with his own wheel mark, and the kiln master counts them as they go in. Perfumer apprenticeship certificate with trade guild attestation is the wheel mark's proof: three-year apprenticeship, 4,000 supervised hours, practical exam, guild dues. A pot that carries a stolen violet cracks in the firing and betrays the thief. The whisper is the price of the broken ware, a whole kiln-load paid to the guild, and the thread is the firing book, kept by the kiln master and read when the pots come out.
